title: Moving to a New Town
description: A girl moves to a new town and slowly makes friends.
instructions: Read the text about moving to a new town, then choose the best answer (A, B, C or D) for each question.

paragraphs.text: In March, Sofia's family moved from a big city to a small town by the sea. Her mother got a new job at the hospital there. Sofia was twelve, and she did not want to leave her old school. She cried when she said goodbye to her best friend, Clara.

The first week at the new school was difficult. Sofia did not know anyone, and she ate her lunch alone. The other students were not unkind, but they already had their own friends. In the evenings, she called Clara and talked for a long time.

Then the music teacher asked Sofia to join the school choir. At the first practice, a girl called Nadia sat next to her. Nadia was also new in town, and she loved singing too. They walked home together after practice and laughed all the way.

Now Sofia has three good friends, and she likes her new town. On Saturdays, they swim in the sea or ride their bikes along the beach. She still calls Clara every week. In the summer, Clara is coming to stay with her for a week.

In July, Clara arrived by train for her visit. Sofia showed her the little harbour, the market and her favourite ice cream shop. Clara was surprised because the town was so quiet and clean. 'It is much nicer than I thought,' she said. Nadia and the other girls took Clara to the beach, and they all became friends quickly.

One evening, Clara asked Sofia a question. 'Do you want to come back to the city?' Sofia thought for a long time. She missed the big shops and her old school a little. But she loved the sea, her new friends and the choir. 'No,' she said. 'I think this is my home now.'

At the end of the week, Sofia and her mother took Clara to the station. The two girls hugged and promised to write letters, not only messages. Clara is going to come again at Christmas, and Sofia is going to visit the city in the spring. On the way home, Sofia's mother smiled. 'You were so sad in March,' she said. 'Now look at you!'
